title: The library
opening:
I don't want the part about the library lost between my pages.

On Tuesday, you wrote:

“Wrote a list and then lost it at the library.”

Then on Wednesday, you wrote:

“The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.”

Come in. I've kept the rest, too.
closing:
I'm putting this bit where I can find it again.

On Wednesday, you wrote:

“The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.”

I can close my covers now. This part is kept.

title: Heard Someone Practising
opening:
No. This bit stays.

On Friday, you wrote:

“Heard someone practising the trumpet on my lunch break.”

Then on Sunday, you wrote:

“Ate lunch on a bench facing the wrong way in the rain.”

I'm opening here. The rest is waiting inside.
closing:
This is where these pages stop.

On Tuesday, you wrote:

“Frost on the car roof in the shape of a map of somewhere that doesn't exist.”

I don't have to know what happens next to keep this.

title: The river
opening:
I want this one right at the front.

On Saturday, you wrote:

“the river, going gold”

Then on Sunday, you wrote:

“Sat with Amanda while she waited for news by the river.”

I'm opening here. The rest is waiting inside.
closing:
I don't want this part falling out when I shut.

On Tuesday, you wrote:

“That I missed writing in here on the two days I didn't.”

I can close my covers now. This part is kept.

title: The table
opening:
I want this one right at the front.

On Tuesday, you wrote:

“I miss Dad. I still put two cups on the table.”

I'm showing you what I have.
closing:
I'm stopping here. The words stay.

That Tuesday page is the last of your words I have from this week.

I can close my covers now. This part is kept.
